import unittest

class Behavior(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_contract(self):
        from patterns import matches
        cases = [('report.txt','*.txt',True), ('.txt','*.txt',True), ('x.txt','*.txt',True),
                 ('report.csv','*.txt',False), ('','',True), ('','*',True), ('','**',True),
                 ('','?',False), ('abc','',False), ('abc','a*c',True), ('ac','a*c',True),
                 ('abbc','a?c',False), ('abc','a?c',True), ('abcd','a*d',True),
                 ('abcd','a*c',False), ('a.b','a.b',True), ('axb','a.b',False),
                 ('cab','a*',False), ('abc','*b*',True), ('abc','***',True),
                 ('图😀','??',True), ('ab\ncd','a*d',True)]
        cases.extend([('[ab]','[ab]',True), ('a','[ab]',False),
                      ('a/b','a?b',True), ('a/b','a*b',True)])
        for name, pattern, expected in cases:
            with self.subTest(name=name, pattern=pattern):
                result = matches(name, pattern)
                self.assertIs(type(result), bool)
                self.assertEqual(result, expected)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# artifact-name-pattern

matches(name, pattern) returns a bool for a full-string match. In pattern, '*' matches zero or more Unicode characters and '?' matches exactly one. Every other character is literal; there is no escape syntax or path separator rule. Empty strings are valid. Keep the existing dynamic-programming approach; the defect is in the '*' transition in matches.
